analysis.investment_thesis: Affle 3i possesses the cleanest financial profile of the five stocks — negligible debt (D/E 0.01), 5/5 years of positive OCF, consistently positive free cash flow, and seven years of unbroken profit growth — qualities I genuinely respect, but the market charges 47.2x earnings and 6.32x book value for them, implying perfection must be delivered indefinitely. My Graham Number of approximately INR 376 versus the INR 1,468 market price means investors pay 3.9x intrinsic value.
key_strengths: Seven consecutive years of rising net profit (INR 28 Cr in 2018 → INR 382 Cr in 2025, 45.3% CAGR) and 5/5 years OCF-positive — the earnings track record I require is firmly established
Net debt is effectively zero (INR 38 Cr borrowings vs INR 1,047 Cr cash) — balance sheet can absorb any foreseeable adversity without equity dilution
Consistently positive free cash flow (INR 266 Cr in 2025) — the business generates genuine surplus capital, not just accounting profits
key_risks: P/E of 47.2x and P/B of 6.32x require continued high growth to justify; any deceleration in India's mobile advertising market would trigger severe re-rating
Operating margin of 18.1% in a technology intermediary business is not exceptional — programmatic ad platforms face structural margin pressure from platform consolidation (Google, Meta)
Acquisitive growth model (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) inflates goodwill/intangibles and obscures organic earnings power — the Investing CF shows –INR 572 Cr in 2024
red_flags: P/B of 6.32 — I pay no more than 1.5× book; at 6× book I have no asset protection if the growth thesis falters
Other Income contributed INR 94 Cr in 2025 (25% of net profit) — quality of earnings is diluted by non-operating items
Revenue CAGR of 45% is built partly through serial acquisitions, not purely organic growth — acquisition accounting can mask true earning power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Affle is the most financially disciplined business in this group by my standards: no meaningful debt, real free cash flow, and a clean seven-year earnings record. In a better-priced market I would study it closely. However, the discipline that made me successful demands I never pay more than a reasonable multiple of proven earning power, and 47 times earnings does not qualify as reasonable under any interpretation of my methodology.

The mobile advertising intermediary business is inherently subject to disruption — Apple's ATT changes, Google's cookie deprecation, and the growing dominance of in-app walled gardens can compress margins without warning. At P/E 47, any such compression would be devastating to the stock price. The Graham Number calculation (~INR 376) tells the whole story: the market price embeds eight to ten years of continued flawless execution. I prefer situations where even mediocre execution produces a satisfactory outcome. This is not one.
